name: Brian Eno
description:
'''Brian Eno''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|iː|n|oʊ}} {{Respell|EE|no}}; born '''Brian Peter George Eno''', 15 May 1948) is an English musician, songwriter, [[record producer]], visual artist, sound designer and political activist. He is known for his pioneering contributions to [[ambient music|ambient]] and [[electronic music]], and for producing, recording, and writing works in [[rock music|rock]] and [[pop music]]. He has been described as one of popular music's most influential and innovative figures. In 2019, he was inducted into the [[Rock and Roll Hall of Fame]] as a member of [[Roxy Music]].

Born in [[Melton, Suffolk]], Eno studied painting and [[experimental music]] at [[Ipswich]] Civic College's art school in the mid-1960s, and then at the [[Winchester School of Art]]. He joined Roxy Music as their keyboardist in 1971, contributing to their first two albums, and left in 1973. With the guitarist [[Robert Fripp]], he recorded ''[[(No Pussyfooting)]]'' (1973) using [[Delay (audio effect)|tape-delay]] and [[reel-to-reel]] loops. In 1974, Eno released his first solo albums, ''[[Here Come the Warm Jets]]'' and ''[[Taking Tiger Mountain (By Strategy)]]''. Eno released the genre-fusing ''[[Another Green World]]'' (1975) the following year, which has been described as "a universally acknowledged masterpiece". Concluding his pop and rock run, he released the [[Oblique Strategies]]-inspired album ''[[Before and After Science]]'' in December 1977. At this time, Eno began to compose and release [[minimal music|minimalist]] music via classically-constructed electronic composition. Several albums exemplifying this approach include ''[[Discreet Music]]'' (1975), Fripp & Eno's ''[[Evening Star (Fripp & Eno album)|Evening Star]]'' (1975), the [[Dieter Moebius|Moebius]]-[[Roedelius]] collaborations ''[[Cluster & Eno]]'' (1977) and ''[[After the Heat]]'' (1978), and ''[[Music for Films]]'' (1978).

During 1978, Eno recorded electronic music intended to be both compositive-friendly and "as ignorable as possible". The result was the start of the ''Ambient'' series, ''[[Ambient 1: Music for Airports]]'' (1979), an album credited with coining the term "ambient music", and described as the greatest in the genre's history by [[Pitchfork (website)|Pitchfork]]. He went on to record the second part with [[Harold Budd]], ''[[The Plateaux of Mirror]]'' (1980). After producing the [[Laraaji]]-released third instalment ''[[Day of Radiance]]'' (1980), Eno released ''[[On Land]]'' in 1982, the last of the series''.'' Eno, along with his brother [[Roger Eno|Roger]] and [[Daniel Lanois]], released ''[[Apollo: Atmospheres and Soundtracks]]'' (1983), the ambient-driven soundtrack of the delayed [[NASA]] film ''[[For All Mankind (film)|For All Mankind]]'' (1989).

Eno has been a producer and occasional backing musician for several artists since the start of his career. [[David Bowie]], an admirer of Eno's work, recruited Eno in his production line-up in Berlin. Those recorded in Berlin ([[Low (David Bowie album)|''Low'']] (1977), [["Heroes" (album)|''"Heroes"'']] (1977) (which also featured Robert Fripp), and [[Lodger (album)|''Lodger'']] (1979)), in what became known as the [[Berlin Trilogy]], became some of Bowie's most acclaimed material. Eno became [[Talking Heads]]' co-producer in 1978, producing ''[[More Songs About Buildings and Food]]'' (1978), ''[[Fear of Music]]'' (1979) and ''[[Remain in Light]]'' (1980); the latter has been called [[List of 1980s albums considered the best|one of the greatest albums]]. He and Daniel Lanois were also [[U2]]'s head producers, producing ''[[The Unforgettable Fire]]'' (1984), ''[[The Joshua Tree]]'' (1987), and ''[[Achtung Baby]]'' (1991). He became a producer and writer for [[Coldplay]] in 2007, producing their album ''[[Viva la Vida or Death and All His Friends]]'' (2008) and co-writing all of ''[[Mylo Xyloto]]'' (2011).

Eno has also collaborated with [[John Cale]], [[Devo]], [[Peter Gabriel]] and [[Genesis (band)|Genesis]], [[David Byrne]], [[Slowdive]], [[James (band)|James]], [[Laurie Anderson]], [[Robert Wyatt]], [[Grace Jones]], [[Karl Hyde]], and [[Fred Again]]. An advocate for [[humanitarian]] causes, Eno writes on a variety of subjects and is a founding member of the [[Long Now Foundation]]. He is an activist on behalf of [[Environmentalism|environmental]], [[anti-war]] and [[pro-Palestinian]] causes.
